capsicum_chilli___Anthracnose.cause: Fungus (Colletotrichum capsici), also called fruit rot and die-back
symptoms: Infection usually begins at flowering: flowers dry up and drop in large numbers.
Tender twigs die from the tip backwards, and the drying spreads to branches and the stem.
On ripe fruit turning red, small black circular spots appear; badly diseased fruit turns straw-coloured.
Partly affected plants bear few fruits, of low quality.
treatment: Three sprayings give good control: Ziram 0.25%, Captan 0.2% or Miltox 0.2%.
Wettable sulphur 0.2%, copper oxychloride 0.25% and Zineb 0.15% also reduced the disease and increased fruit yield.
Spray first just before flowering, again when fruit forms, and a third time a fortnight after the second.
prevention: Treat seed with Thiram or Captan at 4 g per kg to remove infection carried on the seed.

sources.title: Chilli: Fruit Rot and Die Back, TNAU Agritech Portal

symptoms: Leaves show small circular or irregular, dark brown or black greasy spots.
As spots enlarge, the centre becomes lighter, surrounded by a dark band.
Badly affected leaves turn yellow and fall off.
Fruits develop round, raised, water-soaked spots with a pale yellow border.
treatment: Spray mancozeb at 2 g per litre or copper oxychloride at 2.5 g per litre.
Seedlings may be sprayed with Bordeaux mixture 1% or copper oxychloride 0.25%.
Do not spray streptomycin once fruits begin to form.
prevention: Keep the field clean of infected plant material.
Take seed only from disease-free plants.

sources.title: Chilli: Bacterial leaf spot, TNAU Agritech Portal

symptoms: Leaf spots are brown and circular, with small to large light grey centres and dark brown edges.
Spots may grow to 1 cm or more and sometimes merge.
Spots on stems, leaf stalks and pods are elliptical with light grey centres and dark borders.
treatment: Spray twice, 10 to 15 days apart, with Mancozeb 0.25% or Chlorothalonil 0.1%.
capsicum_chilli___Cercospora_leaf_spot.severity: Badly infected leaves drop early, which reduces yield.

sources.title: Chilli: Cercospora leaf spot, TNAU Agritech Portal

symptoms: Leaves curl towards the midrib and become deformed.
Plants are stunted, with shortened stem sections and much smaller leaves.
Flower buds drop before reaching full size.
treatment: There is no known cure for most viral diseases; mechanical and cultural methods are recommended.
Uproot infected plants as soon as they are noticed and burn or bury them.
Controlling the whitefly that carries the virus helps; the source recommends systemic insecticide sprays of Dimethoate 2 ml or Acephate 1 g per litre of water.
prevention: Cover nursery beds with nylon net or straw to protect seedlings.
Raise 2 to 3 rows of maize or sorghum as a border crop to restrict insect carriers.
Avoid growing chilli as a monoculture.

sources.title: Chilli: Viral diseases (leaf curl), TNAU Agritech Portal
